item.title: ‘How do you feel?’: Lindsey Graham again blames India over Russian oil trade
item.description: US Senator Lindsey Graham has warned India and other nations against purchasing Russian oil, alleging it fuels Moscow's war efforts in Ukraine. His remarks followed a deadly Russian missile strike on Kyiv, resulting in numerous casualties, including children. Graham asserted that these countries are experiencing the consequences of supporting Putin, with more repercussions to follow.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Poison in mind’: Trump’s crackdown on gender identity; says revise curriculum or face grant cuts
item.description: The Trump administration instructed the Alabama Department of Public Health to revise its sex education curriculum. Federal officials stated that the curriculum included content related to gender identity. They said this content was outside the scope of the federal Personal Responsibility Education Program. The administration said that federal funds should not promote ideological agendas.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: F-16 crash in Poland: Pilot killed during airshow rehearsal; 'great loss for armed forces', says govt
item.description: A Polish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a rehearsal for an airshow in Radom, central Poland, resulting in the tragic death of the pilot. Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz and Prime Minister Donald Tusk expressed their condolences, honouring the pilot's service and sacrifice. The aircraft belonged to the 31st Tactical Air Base near Poznań.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Minneapolis church shooting: Kennedy flags ‘black box’ drugs; trans meds for violence
item.description: Following a school shooting in Minnesota involving a transgender shooter with a history of mental health struggles, the NIH is launching studies to investigate potential links between psychiatric medications, including SSRIs and drugs used in gender transition, and violent behavior. Secretary Kennedy announced the initiative, highlighting black box warnings on some SSRIs regarding suicidal and homicidal ideation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US says no new visas: Trump not opening doors to 600,000 Chinese students; White House clarifies policy
item.description: The White House clarified that President Trump is not increasing student visas for Chinese nationals, despite recent speculation. The 600,000 figure cited refers to a two-year cumulative count, representing a continuation of existing policy. This clarification addresses criticism from those who viewed the number as a policy shift amid ongoing US-China trade negotiations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Not happy, not surprised’: Trump unsurprised by deadly Russian strikes on Kyiv, White House calls for de-escalation
item.description: White House reports Donald Trump's reaction to Russia's Kyiv strikes. He was not happy but not surprised. The strikes resulted in casualties and hit civilian targets. Karoline Leavitt mentioned Ukraine's recent actions against Russian oil refineries. Trump wants a negotiated resolution. Keith Kellogg warned the attacks could hinder peace efforts. The administration claims ongoing diplomatic efforts to end the conflict.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘People are desperate’: Trump threatens federal takeover of Chicago; blasts governor Pritzker over rising crime
item.description: US President Donald Trump has intensified his criticism of Illinois Governor JB Pritzker over rising gun violence in Chicago, hinting at potential federal intervention. Trump cited recent shootings and murders, questioning Pritzker's ability to manage the crisis. He suggested federal assistance could be necessary, echoing past deployments in other cities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Living in terror’: Trump’s law enforcement surge sparks anxiety in DC - mayor Bowser raises concerns
item.description: Mayor Muriel Bowser voices concerns over rising anxiety in Washington, DC, particularly among immigrant communities, due to the federal law enforcement surge. While acknowledging a decrease in crime, she criticizes the presence of masked ICE agents and out-of-state National Guard troops, highlighting residents' fear of being caught in a "dragnet.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet the top 10 longest-lived people in the world and see how they lived over 100 years
item.description: This article explores the remarkable lives of the world's ten longest-lived individuals, including Jeanne Calment, who lived to 122. It examines their nationalities, ages, and lifestyle choices, such as diet, social engagement, and mental well-being. The insights reveal common threads like strong family support, positive attitudes, and active lifestyles that contribute to exceptional longevity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Egregious’: Russia's attack on Ukraine receives backlash- Here's what nations said
item.description: A major Russian air assault on Kyiv resulted in at least 18 deaths and 48 injuries, drawing international condemnation. The EU diplomatic offices were damaged in the attack. Despite the strikes, Russia claims to be open for diplomacy, while continuing to target Ukraine's military infrastructure. The EU and UK summoned Russian envoys, denouncing the strikes, which threaten ongoing peace efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Robin Westman: MAGA Is blaming Ilhan Omar for the Minneapolis shooting; and weaponizing the trans-identity
item.description: Following the tragic shooting at Annunciation Catholic School in Minneapolis, which resulted in the deaths of two children and injuries to seventeen others, MAGA-aligned figures have swiftly attempted to politicize the event. They are baselessly blaming Representative Ilhan Omar, pushing a narrative of a 'Red-Green alliance' despite the absence of any evidence linking the shooter to Omar or her politics.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Robin Westman: Candace Owens floats ridiculous theory; calls Minneapolis shooting 'govt psyop'
item.description: Into this grief stepped Candace Owens. Within hours of the attack, she posted on social media that the government was behind the shooting. “Each shooting is more traumatizing than the last,” she wrote, “because the goal is to scare us into compliance. It is the tried and true strategy of 9/11 and the Manson murders—both CIA operations. Do not ever agree to hand over your 2nd amendment rights.”
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: How rich is Dubai Princess Sheikha Mahra? Inside the royal's net worth, and how she makes her money
item.description: Sheikha Mahra of Dubai, daughter of the UAE ruler, commands a personal net worth estimated between $300 million and $1.5 billion. Beyond royal inheritance, her wealth stems from her luxury brand Mahra M1, launched after a high-profile divorce. With bold business moves and a global engagement to rapper French Montana, she’s shaping a modern, independent royal identity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kim Jong Un to visit China: First public appearance at multilateral event in 6 years; Russia also attending
item.description: Kim Jong Un will visit China for a military parade, marking his first major multilateral event appearance. Alongside Putin, Kim's presence highlights a growing alignment between North Korea, China, and Russia amid US alliance-building in Asia. The visit signals potential shifts in international relations and could pave the way for renewed negotiations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE’s humanitarian mission: Rescue team flies Black Hawk missions to combat Albania’s forest fires
item.description: The UAE rescue team is providing crucial assistance to Albania by combating the ongoing forest fires. Utilizing Black Hawk helicopters, the team has conducted 27 aerial missions, delivering over 1,261 tons of water to critical hotspots. These targeted water drops, coordinated with Albanian officials, aim to contain the blazes in regions like Gramsh, Ballolli, and Vlorë, amidst challenging conditions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ukraine allows young men to leave the country: Why Kyiv is suddenly easing its wartime travel ban
item.description: Ukraine is easing wartime travel restrictions, allowing men aged 18-22 to travel abroad until 23, effective August 29, 2025. This reverses the blanket ban imposed in 2022. Kyiv aims to provide educational and employment opportunities, addressing demographic challenges worsened by the war.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US Army is using TikTok to recruit young soldiers: How influencers are selling military life to Gen Z
item.description: The US Army is strategically utilizing TikTok to engage Gen Z for recruitment, despite security concerns surrounding the platform. Young soldiers and veterans are sharing engaging content, highlighting benefits like education and camaraderie. This shift aims to modernize the Army's image, using relatable influencers to overcome skepticism towards traditional recruitment methods.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: This Australian island has the world’s most beautiful airport landing and its runway begins in the ocean
item.description: Lord Howe Island Airport in Australia has been named the world's most beautiful airport landing. A recent study using eye-tracking technology revealed that its unique ocean-to-beach runway captured travellers' attention more than any other airport.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Qatar: Arriving in Doha? Hamad International Airport shares key tips for stress-free entry
item.description: Hamad International Airport (HIA) has updated arrival procedures for the end of summer, focusing on efficient transportation and baggage handling. Passengers are encouraged to use parking facilities for pick-ups and utilize various transport options like Uber, Doha Metro, and taxis. E-gates are available for eligible travelers, ensuring a smoother immigration process.
